front.zh: 現代俳句 & 變奏   系列《44》

zh: 莊子說  : 天地有大美而不言
en: Tonight, the starry sky is very Greek, imagine
God said: let there be light, and there was light
Zhuangzi said: heaven and earth possess great beauty yet speak not of it

points.zh:
姑且步黑暗的龍脊而下
用觸覺透視
也可以走完這一列中世紀
小葉和聰聰
撥開你長睫上重重的夜
就發現神話很守時
星空，非常希臘
--余光中 《 重上大度山 》1961
舊約聖經    創世紀第一章:  1 ~ 5 節。
「起初神創造天地。地是空虛混沌，淵面黑暗。神的靈運行在水面上神說，要有光，就有了光。神看光是好的，就把光暗分開了。神稱光為晝，稱暗為夜，有晚上，有早晨，這是頭一日。」
天地有大美而不言，四時有明法而不議，萬物有成理而不說。      --莊子《知北遊》

en: Within the book there is truly----
On the left page, the stream's floating light in scattered points
On the right page, a fishing boat drifts silently away
I am a pawn, having crossed the Chu River
Songs of Chu gradually rise, and I do not know
Tonight, where shall I lodge

points.zh: 胡適名言: 「做了過河卒子，只好拼命向前。」
points.en: A famous saying of Hu Shih: "Once you've become a pawn that has crossed the river, all you can do is push forward with all your might."

en: Outside the car, a great cluster
Cosmos flowers, blooming in riotous color
The glorious history of Cyrus

points.zh: 公元前550年，居魯士帶領波斯人攻克了當時西亞三大強國之一的米底，正式建立波斯帝國。居魯士屬於波斯人的阿契美尼德家族，因此他所創立的帝國也被稱為阿契美尼德王朝。公元前539年，波斯攻陷千古名城——巴比倫城，居魯士把都城遷往巴比倫。至此波斯已經從一個城邦發展為一個洲際大帝國，成為歷史上第一個地跨亞非歐三大洲的大帝國。居魯士寬容的政治政策也使波斯成為了上古中東諸文明的集大成者。波斯帝國的出現更是世界歷史的一個輝煌篇章的總結。公元前334年，波斯帝國大流士三世被亞歷山大帝征服而淪亡。

zh: 波斯菊，學名及英文俗名Cosmos，源於希腊語，意爲秩序、和諧、世界、宇宙，而英語中表示“宇宙”的詞語也源於這希腊語。故波斯菊又有“ 宇宙之花“ 的美稱。
en: The cosmos flower's scientific and common English name, Cosmos, derives from the Greek, meaning order, harmony, world, universe — and the English word for 'universe' likewise derives from this same Greek root. Hence the cosmos flower also carries the beautiful name 'flower of the universe.'
Walking to where the water ends
Asking the wind, may I
keep me in the picture.

flow.caption_zh: Gemini AI對這首俳句的解讀:

points.zh:
這三行詩展現了一種極致的孤獨感，卻又帶著一種卑微而優雅的執著。它融合了東方的禪意哲思與西方的現代感性，形成了一種跨時空的對話。
1. 境遇的終點：「行到水窮處」
這句引用自王維的《終南別業》: 「行到水窮處，坐看雲起時。」
字面意義： 走到水源的盡頭，路消失了，水也不見了。
深層隱喻： 代表了一種絕境或人生的轉折點。在傳統詩詞中，下一句通常是「坐看雲起時」，代表一種豁達與隨緣。但在此詩中，詩人並沒有轉向雲淡風輕，而是轉向了「風」。
2. 對話的對象：「對風說」
不穩定性： 風是抓不住的、流動的、無形的。對風說話，暗示了身邊已無人傾聽，或者說，詩人所求訴的對象就像風一樣，隨時會離去。
孤寂的姿態： 在水盡之處對著虛無的風開口，這是一種極致的荒涼感。
3. 核心的訴求：「Keep me in the picture」
這是一句充滿現代感的英文，打破了前兩句建立的古風意境，產生了強烈的衝擊力：
渴望被記得： 「Keep me in the picture」原意是「讓我也知情」或「別把我排除在外」。在這裡，它更像是在乞求：即便世界在變遷、你在流動，請在你的生命藍圖中，為我保留一個位置。
定格的欲望： 詩人走到水源盡頭，感受到了消失的恐懼。他不想就此被遺忘，因此拜託那唯一還在流動的「風」，將他的身影留存。
總結與意境
這首詩描寫的是一種「即便走到盡頭，仍不願放手」的心境。
它把王維那種「隨遇而安」的禪意，轉化成了現代人對存在感的焦慮與渴望。詩人站在荒蕪的盡頭，面對著注定會離開的「風」（可能是愛人、時光或命運），卑微地請求：「請不要在你的世界裡，抹去我的身影。」
這是一種很美、卻也讓人感到心碎的倔強。
這首詩本身就像風裡的一句低聲私語，很耐讀。
points.en:
These three lines of poetry convey a sense of utter solitude, yet also a humble and graceful persistence. They fuse Eastern Zen philosophy with Western modern sensibility, creating a dialogue across time and space.
1. The end of the road: "Walking to where the water ends"
This line is drawn from Wang Wei's "My Retreat at Mount Zhongnan": "I walk to where the water ends, and sit and watch the clouds rise."
Literal meaning: Walking to the very source of the water, the path disappears, and the water itself vanishes.
Deeper metaphor: This represents a dead end, or a turning point in life. In the traditional poem, the next line is usually "and sit and watch the clouds rise," representing an open-minded acceptance of whatever comes. But in this poem, the poet does not turn toward serene clouds — instead turns toward the "wind."
2. The object of address: "speaking to the wind"
Instability: Wind cannot be grasped — it is flowing and formless. Speaking to the wind implies that there is no longer anyone nearby to listen, or that the one the poet appeals to is, like the wind, liable to leave at any moment.
A posture of solitude: To open one's mouth to the empty wind at the very place the water ends is an image of utter desolation.
3. The core plea: "Keep me in the picture"
This is a thoroughly modern English phrase that breaks the classical mood established by the first two lines, producing a striking impact:
A longing to be remembered: "Keep me in the picture" originally means "let me know too" or "don't leave me out." Here it feels more like a plea: even as the world changes and you move on, please keep a place for me somewhere in the blueprint of your life.
The desire to be fixed in place: Having walked to where the water ends, the poet feels the fear of vanishing. Unwilling to be forgotten, he begs the wind — the only thing still moving — to preserve his image.
Summary and mood
This poem depicts a state of mind that refuses to let go even at the very end of the road.
It transforms Wang Wei's Zen spirit of 'accepting what comes' into a modern person's anxiety and longing for a sense of existence. Standing at the desolate end of the road, facing the wind — which is bound to leave (perhaps representing a lover, time, or fate) — the poet humbly pleads: "Please do not erase my presence from your world."
It is a beautiful yet heartbreaking kind of stubbornness.
The poem itself is like a soft whisper carried on the wind — well worth savoring.

en: Sitting idly at dusk
Half a bottle of Heineken, poured out
Old memories, long since settled
There is always that one instant
Fog, as though spreading without ever dispersing
Then, let us view the flowers through mist!
Then let this mood be so
Slipping into last night's wind and rain
Fallen blossoms cover the ground

zh: 一點點就好，百香綠茶的糖
一點點就好，壽司上的芥末
一點點就好，你眼角的閃光
en: Just a little will do -- the sugar in passionfruit green tea
Just a little will do -- the wasabi on the sushi
Just a little will do -- the glint at the corner of your eye
Come, sit quietly with me
Watching the distant river valley, where mist and cloud rise
Asking you, when will you come back?

points.zh:
《 Red River Valley 》
Canadian folk song, 1896
From this valley they say you are leaving
We shall miss your bright eyes and sweet smile
For you take with you all of the sunshine
That has brightened our pathway a while
Then come sit by my side if you love me
Do not hasten to bid me adieu
Just remember the Red River Valley
And the cowboy that's loved you so true
